name: Dialogs
doc:
A library providing dialogs for interacting with users.

`Dialogs` is Robot Framework's standard library that provides means
for pausing the test or task execution and getting input from users.

Long lines in the provided messages are wrapped automatically. If you want
to wrap lines manually, you can add newlines using the `\n` character
sequence.

keywords.name: Execute Manual Step
keywords.doc:
Pauses execution until user sets the keyword status.

User can press either `PASS` or `FAIL` button. In the latter case execution
fails and an additional dialog is opened for defining the error message.
keywords.shortdoc: Pauses execution until user sets the keyword status.

args.name: message
args.doc: The instruction shown in the initial dialog.

args.name: default_error
args.doc:
The default value shown in the possible error message
dialog.

keywords.name: Get Selection From User
keywords.doc:
Pauses execution and asks user to select a value.

The selected value is returned. Pressing `Cancel` fails the keyword.

Example:

```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Select User
    ${user} =    Get Selection From User    Select user    user1    user2    admin
    ${user} =    Get Selection From User    Select user    user1    user2    admin    default=user1
    ${user} =    Get Selection From User    Select user    user1    user2    admin    default=1
```

`default` is new in Robot Framework 7.1.
keywords.shortdoc: Pauses execution and asks user to select a value.

args.name: message
args.doc: The instruction shown in the dialog.

args.name: values
args.doc: The options given to the user.

args.name: default
args.doc:
Optional default value. Can either be one of the specified
values or the index of the value starting from `1`. For example,
`default=user1` and `default=1` in the examples below have the
exact same effect.

keywords.returnDoc: The value selected by the user.

keywords.name: Get Selections From User
keywords.doc:
Pauses execution and asks user to select multiple values.

The selected values are returned as a list. Selecting no values is OK
and in that case the returned list is empty. Pressing `Cancel` fails
the keyword.

Example:

```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Select Users
    ${users} =    Get Selections From User    Select users    user1    user2    admin
```
keywords.shortdoc: Pauses execution and asks user to select multiple values.

args.name: message
args.doc: The instruction shown in the dialog.

args.name: values
args.doc: The options given to the user.

keywords.returnDoc: The values selected by the user as a list. Empty if nothing was selected.

keywords.name: Get Value From User
keywords.doc:
Pauses execution and asks user to input a value.

Value typed by the user, or the possible default value, is returned.
Returning an empty value is fine, but pressing `Cancel` fails the keyword.

Example:

```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Get Credentials
    ${username} =    Get Value From User    Input username    default
    ${password} =    Get Value From User    Input password    hidden=yes
```
keywords.shortdoc: Pauses execution and asks user to input a value.

args.name: message
args.doc: The instruction shown in the dialog.

args.name: default_value
args.doc: The possible default value shown in the input field.

args.name: hidden
args.doc: If given a true value, the value typed by the user is hidden.

keywords.returnDoc: Value typed by the user, or the default value.

keywords.name: Pause Execution
keywords.doc: Pauses execution until user clicks `Ok` button.
keywords.shortdoc: Pauses execution until user clicks `Ok` button.

args.name: message
args.doc: The message shown in the dialog.
args.defaultValue: Execution paused. Press OK to continue.
args.repr: message: str = Execution paused. Press OK to continue.

typedocs.name: boolean
typedocs.doc:
Strings `TRUE`, `YES`, `ON`, `1` and possible localization specific "true strings"
are converted to Boolean `True`, the empty string, strings `FALSE`, `NO`, `OFF`
and `0` and possibly localization specific "false strings" are converted to
Boolean `False`, and the string `NONE` is converted to the Python `None` object.
Other strings and all other values are passed as-is, allowing keywords to handle
them specially if needed.

All string comparisons are case-insensitive.

Examples: `TRUE` (converted to `True`), `off` (converted to `False`), `example`
(used as-is)

typedocs.name: integer
typedocs.doc:
Conversion is done using Python's [int] built-in function. Floating point numbers
are accepted only if they can be represented as integers exactly. For example,
`1.0` is accepted but `1.1` is not.

It is possible to use hexadecimal, octal and binary numbers by prefixing values
with `0x`, `0o` and `0b`, respectively.

Spaces and underscores can be used as visual separators for digit grouping purposes.

Examples: `42`, `-1`, `0b1010`, `10 000 000`, `0xBAD_C0FFEE`

[int]: https://docs.python.org/library/functions.html#int

typedocs.name: None
typedocs.doc:
String `NONE` (case-insensitive) and the empty string are converted to the Python
`None` object. Other values cause an error.

Converting the empty string is new in Robot Framework 7.4.

typedocs.name: string
typedocs.doc:
All arguments are converted to Unicode strings.

Most values are converted simply by using `str(value)`. An exception is that
bytes are mapped directly to Unicode code points with same ordinals. This means
that, for example, `b"hyv\xe4"` becomes `"hyvä"`.

Converting bytes specially is new Robot Framework 7.4.
